properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. dev_storyflow, 2026-09-08, three observations from the session that could not reach reflow2 at all — the one the version-guard bug locked out.

**Opportunity, in their words:** "RCA output has nowhere to go when the server is down. This session produced a full root-cause analysis with five candidates, three of them refuted by measurement against production. All of it is prose in a terminal. If the export format could accept an offline-recorded node batch for later reconciliation, that work would not be lost."

**Gap, same session:** "a `/where` answered from the export cannot report gaps. Open gap counts are computed by `detect_gaps` at call time and are not materialised as nodes, so an export-based `/where` can report capability/requirement status but is structurally blind to the one number the Stop hook nudges about. The hook told me '286 → 291 (+5)' and I could not refresh or verify it. Worth considering whether the export should carry a stamped gap count so a degraded session can at least say how stale its number is."

**And, from the same file but with the server UP:** "Findings about the RUNNING system have nowhere to go. This session measured a lot of durable truth about production: the per-session notes listing route does not exist (404), note creation does (32 notes live on Errat)... None of that is a Requirement, Capability, Artifact or Decision. `link-artifacts` records files; `capture-session` records reasoning; there is no home for 'I probed the deployed system and here is what is true of it today.'"

⚠️ THE THIRD ONE MAY BE REFUTABLE AND WAS NOT CHECKED. They list four types and do not mention `TemporalFact`, which is dated, carries `basis: measured`, has a `subject_id`, and is what `record_finding` writes. If that is the home, this is a DISCOVERABILITY gap rather than a vocabulary one — the same shape as three of their eight Verification wishes turning out to be already built. **Not verified here, because it needs their graph and their reading, not mine.**

═══ WHY THE THREE ARE ONE QUESTION ═══

Each is a session holding something true that the design cannot receive: because the server is down, because the reader is an export rather than a graph, or because the finding is about the world rather than the design. The common shape is that reflow2 assumes the graph is reachable and the subject is internal.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) AN OFFLINE NODE BATCH the export can carry and a later session reconciles.** ⚠️ Counter, and it is serious: a batch written without the graph cannot search first, so it cannot avoid duplicates, cannot draw relations, and cannot meet the near-duplicate guard — every discipline this project has built at capture time is unavailable offline. What arrives later would need the whole guard applied retroactively, which is a merge problem rather than an import.

**(b) STAMP A GAP COUNT INTO THE EXPORT so a degraded reader knows how stale it is.** Small, honest, and it makes a degraded answer say so rather than being silently blind. ⚠️ Counter: a stamped count is a number that is wrong the moment anything changes, and this project has a standing objection to storing what it can compute — a stale count read as current is the failure `claim_age` exists to prevent.

**(c) DO NOTHING FOR (a) AND (b), AND FIX THE CAUSE INSTEAD.** Both only matter because the server was down, and it was down because of a defect now fixed in v0.56.0. ⚠️ Counter, theirs: servers will be down again for other reasons, and "AGENTS.md tells a session with no reflow2 tools to 'say so and stop'; that is the right instruction for design work but it gives no guidance for a session doing live production diagnosis, where stopping would have left the user blocked." **That sentence is the real finding in this cluster** and it is about instructions rather than mechanism.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

Check whether `TemporalFact` already houses "what is true of the deployed system today". If it does, one third of this cluster is a pointing problem and the answer is an instruction, not a type. That is one question to the reporter.
properties.name: OPEN — the degraded-session family: an RCA done while the server is down is lost, a /where from the export is blind to gaps, and findings about the RUNNING system have no home even when it is up
properties.no_relation_note: Searched for the degraded-operation work. Nearest were cmp:degraded with ver:degraded-surface and ver:degraded-follows-transport — but those answer a DIFFERENT failure: the server is UP and the graph is held by another process, so a reduced tool surface can be served and can explain itself. This wish is the case where the server is not reachable at all, where by construction no tool can be served and the session has nowhere to put an RCA it has already done. Also considered dec:idea-how-does-the-graph-learn-what-a-session-invalidated, which is about capture being additive, not about reachability. No real relation to any of them.
